### [S005.U1] PART 1 - GENERAL > 1.3 SYSTEM DESCRIPTION > A. Performance Requirements
1. Formwork Design: Design formwork, shoring and bracing to sustain construction and wind loads and maintain concrete lines and levels within concrete tolerances specified herein. Formwork types are labeled according to concrete surface finishes. Provide formwork types and construction to obtain the class of surface indicated and as required by referenced standards. Design forms to permit easy removal. Make the forms sufficiently rigid and strong enough to withstand, without leakage, the high hydraulic pressures which result from rapid filling and heavy high-frequency vibration. Deflection of each formwork component shall be limited to 1/360 of the component span due to hydraulic pressure of concrete.

### [S008.U6] PART 1 - GENERAL > 1.5 QUALITY ASSURANCE
- H. Pre-Construction Conference: At least 35 days prior to submitting the proposed mix designs, conduct a conference to review the proposed materials, mix designs, construction procedures and finishing systems for the concrete work. Topics to include but are not limited to pour sequence, trade placement sequence, shoring/reshoring sequence, slab surveys, and highlight of all requirements the Contractor or subcontractor has taken exception to. The meeting shall be attended by the ER and representatives of the Testing Agencies and the subcontractors involved with supplying, conveying, placing, finishing, and curing the concrete. Furnish the conference agenda to attendees 20 days prior to the scheduled conference date. Meeting shall include the following:
1. Employer's Representative.
2. Engineer in Charge (ER).
3. General Contractor.
4. Concrete Subcontractor.

5. Independent Testing Agancy.
6. Ready mix concrete supplier.

### [S009.U1] PART 1 - GENERAL > 1.6 DELIVERY, STORAGE AND HANDLING
- A. Packing, Shipping, Handling, and Unloading: Use materials from the same source from start to finish of job unless changes have been accepted by the ER. Deliver and store materials in manufacturer's original packaging labeled to show name, brand, type, and grade. Store, materials in protected dry location off ground in accordance with manufacturer's instructions. stockpile and use aggregate in a manner which minimizes moisture content variation. Concrete producer and suppliers shall load, transport, handle, store and batch concrete materials in a manner that will ensure the materials are not contaminated, unclean, segregated or affected in a way that will damage the final product.

### [S034.U1] PART 2 - PRODUCTS > 2.11 REQUIREMENTS FOR MASS CONCRETE
- A. Mass concrete clauses shall apply to concrete used in Mat Foundations and should be considered for footings greater than 1.0 m thick. Same materials and proportioning as normal weight structural concrete, except use moderate heat of hydration, moderate sulphate resistance cement, water reducing retarding admixture, and crushed ice if necessary to maintain required temperature.

1. Retardation: Minimum 3 hours.
2. Temperature: Maximum 21° C at point of deposit.

### [S049.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE
- A. Concrete is prepared by mixing graded aggregates along with cement, water and approved admixtures, in a specified proportion. Mixing shall be done using a mechanical mixer. Manual hand mixing shall be permitted in specific cases with the written permission of the ER on account of small quantity or location or any other reason acceptable to the ER.

### [S049.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE
- B. Cement Concrete.
1. This shall be classified as plain cement concrete or reinforced cement concrete. Plain cement concrete shall be used in leveling courses under foundations, floors, copings etc. Reinforced cement concrete shall be used typically at all locations.
- a. Concrete shall be classified by its compressive strength at the 28th day. The concrete grades shall be as designated in table 2 of IS 456 and are given as ready reference in Table - 4.

### [S049.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > B. Cement Concrete.
- b. It shall be the responsibility of the Contractor to carry out design mixes and approval of the same shall be obtained from the ER at least 35 days in advance from the actual pouring of concrete at site in the permanent Work. The basic aim of mix design shall be to find the most economic proportion of cement, aggregates and water which will give the desired strength of concrete, proper workability and durability. Also it is important that the mix should be easily worked with the help of equipment available at site. The operations involved at site are, measurement of materials, their mixing, placing, compacting, finishing required and curing. The design shall be carried out strictly to IS specifications and IS code practice 456, SP 23 and SP 24.

### [S049.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > B. Cement Concrete.
- c. The Contractor shall ensure that the minimum cement content per cubic

- meter of reinforced concrete should not be less than that stipulated in table 23, 24, 25 and 26 of SP 23 and Table 5 and Table 6 herein.
- d. For expected strength of cubes tested on the 28 th day the design mix at preliminary test and work site shall be as per IS 456, SP 23 and SP 24. The water cement ratio shall be between 0.5 to 0.52. Additional water may be permitted only at the discretion of the ER. The slump shall be 25 mm to 35 mm depending upon the location and type of Work. Higher slump with use of plasticizers shall be permitted.

### [S049.U5] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE
- C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
1. The Contractor shall submit the mix designs that he proposes to use at site to the ER for review at least 5 weeks in advance of planned use, The mix design shall also give basic details, when tested according to Is 1199 and IS 2386 - Part III, such as.
- a. Slump
- b. Vee - Bee Test

### [S049.U6] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
- c. Bleeding
- d. Cement required for one cubic meter of concrete
- e. Compacting factor
2. On receipt of this, the ER may immediately order a work site test to be performed before the final approval. This shall be done with mixer and materials actually being used at site.
3. 5 cubes shall be taken from each of the 3 batches to test the mix. Cubes shall be cast, stored, cured, transported and tested per IS 516. The test may be carried out at site or laboratory as approved by the ER.

### [S049.U7] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
4. Trial mixes shall be approved provided that average strength of 3 consecutive cubes is not less than that specified and that one out of three may give a value less than specified but limited to a maximum of 90% of the specified strength.
5. In case the trial mix falls below the above criteria, the ER shall order fresh trial mixes to be made as before, until the desired strength is arrived at.

### [S049.U8] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > C. Design Mix And Trial Mixes
6. This design mix and trial mix hold good so long as the materials continue to be of the same quality and from the same sources. For any change, the ER may order fresh design mix and trial mixes to be carried out before the same is used at site.
7. It is the responsibility of the Contractor to prepare and get the cubes tested and to provide all the material, labour, moulds, equipment, casting and curing required.

- d. Slump.
- e. Concrete cube strength.

10. The format of records shall be prepared in consultation with the ER and either he or his representative shall have full access to the Contractor's laboratory..
